question.text: What will be the major product when m-cresol is reacted with propargyl bromide <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>≡</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> in presence of <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> in acetone?

solution.text: The m-cresol is the m-methyl phenol. Phenol is acidic in nature. It gives the acid-base reaction with base. So, when it reacts with the base, it will form the phenolate ion. After that phenolate ion act as a nucleophile. This nucleophile gives the nucleophilic substitution reaction with the alkyl halide. It will follow the SN2 reaction mechanism.
